answers.question: I feel ready. Can I go back to 40 miles next week and start speedwork for the 10K?
answers.answer:
Short answer: not yet. Hold at easy running for one more week, then we start layering structure back in.

Here is how I think about the two weeks after a marathon. Your legs feel springy because the cardio system comes back fast, but tendons, feet and the small stabilisers take three to four weeks to fully reset. Pushing speed in that window is where most post-marathon niggles start.

On mileage, jumping 12 to 40 is a 28-mile step. I would rather build 12, then around 22, then around 30, then 36 to 40 across four weeks. You will still be ready to race a 10K well, and you will stay healthy.

On the Thanksgiving 10K, it is doable: five weeks is enough to add strides, one tempo and one short interval session, and sharpen. If you want to target it, say the word and I will build a short 10K block starting the week of Nov 2. If you would rather rest the competitive brain and just rebuild base, that is a good choice too. Tell me which, and whether you want to think about another marathon in the spring.

new.analysis:
## How the week went
You followed the recovery plan cleanly: three easy runs on the days I planned them, totals right on, and heart rate drifted down to 133 average on the first run and back up to 139 on Sunday as pace returned to 9:51. That is a textbook recovery pattern, and the 0/10 pain all week backs it up.

## Why next week stays easy
You are 14 days out from a 3:50 marathon where you spent 63 percent of the race in zone 4 and the last 10K was a grind on wrecked quads. That damage is not fully gone just because the soreness is. One more easy week protects you from the classic "felt great, got hurt" trap in week three.

## What next week does
It nudges volume from 12 to around 23 miles with a slightly longer Sunday, still all easy, no structure. If everything feels normal through the weekend, the week after that I will add short strides and bring you back toward 30 miles. Tell me your next goal and I will shape the block from there.
